name: Voyageurs National Park
blurb: Wolves, loons and beavers on the lakes and boreal forest of the Canadian Shield.

tip.title: Remove the wolves
tip.text: Wolves hunt deer, beaver and hares. Set Gray wolf to -100% and watch those prey, then the birch, fir and pine they browse.

notes: The story and why it matters come from the Wikipedia articles listed below (Voyageurs National Park, Wolf, Common loon). Individual species and links have not been checked one by one. Feeding links that match a GloBI (Global Biotic Interactions) record are marked in the node details, with a link to the records. A few links were added from GloBI records.

nodes.desc: Summer light drives growth in the park forests and in the algae of its lakes.
The park service describes fire as a long-standing force that renews forests, which are managed today with fire, forest health and visitors in mind.
Break down dead wood, leaves, carcasses and lake sediment, returning nutrients to soil and water.
A pale-barked northern hardwood recorded in the park; browsed by deer, hares and beavers and a common pioneer after disturbance.

nodes.name: Balsam fir
nodes.desc: A boreal conifer of the spruce-fir forest type found in the park; eaten as browse by deer, hares and beavers.

nodes.name: Lowbush blueberry
nodes.desc: A low shrub with berries eaten by black bears and browsed by deer.
Drifting microscopic algae that feed zooplankton at the base of the lake food chain. General ecology.
Abundant in the park; browses birch, fir and pine and is a main prey of wolves and a common carcass for scavengers.
Feeds on birch, fir and pine and builds dams that reshape ponds and wetlands; the park service says beavers transform its ecosystems.
Browses young twigs and bark of birch, fir and pine, and is prey for wolves, bears and eagles.
A forest rodent recorded often in the park that eats conifer seeds and buds and is taken by eagles.

nodes.name: Water fleas (zooplankton)
nodes.desc: Tiny crustaceans that graze phytoplankton and feed small fish. General ecology.

nodes.name: Common loon
nodes.desc: Dives for fish, mostly small ones including perch and walleye; eggs and chicks are taken by eagles, and fluctuating water can flood nests.

nodes.name: River otter
nodes.desc: Hunts fish and waterfowl in the park lakes and wetlands.
A scavenger that feeds on carrion such as winter-killed deer.
An omnivore that eats berries, deer, hares and beavers.
The park top predator, hunting deer and also smaller prey like beaver and hares.

nodes.name: Bald eagle
nodes.desc: A fish-eating raptor that also takes loons, hares and squirrels and scavenges carcasses.

story: Voyageurs National Park in northern Minnesota is known for its water: canoeists, kayakers and anglers use its lakes. The Kabetogama Peninsula, most of its land, can only be reached by boat. The park is named for the French-Canadian fur traders who travelled these waters.
matters: Most of the park is reachable only by boat, or in winter by snowmobile, ski or snowshoe. The Boundary Waters Canoe Area Wilderness lies to its east.
